findings.title: async forEach makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
findings.body: In `Reschedule`, the loop over `bookingRefsFiltered` was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` because `getCalendar` is now async. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so all `calendar.deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` calls are now unawaited: the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true` before deletions finish, and any rejection inside a callback becomes an unhandled promise rejection that the surrounding `try/catch` (which only catches synchronous errors) will never see. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (optionally with per-item catch) so failures are logged and deletions complete before the email is sent.

findings.title: async forEach makes calendar/video deletions fire-and-forget and defeats the try/catch
findings.body: Same issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the loop was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` to await the now-async `getCalendar`, but forEach does not await async callbacks. The booking is already marked CANCELLED and the reschedule email is sent before the calendar/video event deletions complete, and any failure to delete is an unhandled rejection invisible to the surrounding try/catch. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` with individual error handling.

findings.title: requestReschedule no longer awaits calendar/video deletions
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` was introduced because `getCalendar` became async. Since forEach doesn't await its callbacks, the mutation sends the reschedule email, fires webhooks, and returns while the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still pending; a serverless function may be frozen before they finish, leaving stale events on users' calendars, and any errors become unhandled rejections. Await the deletions with `Promise.all(...map(...))`.

findings.title: Recurring-cancellation branch pushes into apiDeletes asynchronously after it is awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-event cancellation path, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` pushes deletion promises into `apiDeletes` from async callbacks. `apiDeletes` is later consumed by `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (and by `await apiDeletes` in the paid branch), both of which run before any of these pushes happen, so the recurring calendar event deletions are never awaited and their results/errors are lost. Cancel can return success while the recurring events remain on the calendar. Collect the deletions with `Promise.all(credentials.map(...))` and push the resulting promises synchronously.

findings.title: appStore values are now Promises; only 6 of its consumers were updated
findings.body: Every entry in the default-exported `appStore` map changed from a module namespace object to a `Promise` via top-level `import(...)`. This is a breaking contract change for every consumer of `@calcom/app-store`, but the PR only updates `getCalendar.ts`, `videoClient.ts`, `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `deletePayment.ts`, and `handlePayment.ts`. Any other file that indexes `appStore[...]` synchronously (e.g. `appStore[appName].lib` or `appStore[key].app`) will now receive a Promise and silently fail checks like `"lib" in app` or crash on property access. The change needs an audit (and ideally a type-level guarantee) that all importers of `@calcom/app-store` await the values.

findings.title: Debug log of CalendarService constructor left in getCalendar
findings.body: `log.info("calendarApp", calendarApp.lib.CalendarService)` logs the CalendarService class constructor on every calendar resolution. This runs on every booking/availability call, adding noisy, low-value log output (and potentially expensive serialization of a class). It looks like a debugging leftover and should be removed or downgraded.
